Class TftTouchShield

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.tft.TftTouchShield
public final class TftTouchShield extends Object
Driver for the ELEGOO 2.8" TFT touch screen shield ("Pantalla Táctil TFT de 2,8 pulgadas"): a 240x320 ILI9341 display on an 8-bit parallel bus, a 4-wire resistive touch panel, and a microSD socket, wired for the shield's standard UNO pinout as used by ELEGOO's Elegoo_TFTLCD and TouchScreen libraries.

Like LcdKeypadShield, this shield needs no new compiler intrinsic: every operation is built from Gpio.pinMode(int, int), Gpio.digitalWrite(int, boolean), Gpio.analogRead(int), and Delay. The price is speed — each bus byte costs a handful of digitalWrite calls, so clearing the whole screen takes on the order of a second while drawing a line of text takes tens of milliseconds. That suits status screens and simple UIs, not animation. The driver only rewrites data pins whose level actually changes, so solid fills in colors whose two bytes are equal (e.g. BLACK, WHITE) are the fastest.

The SD socket is an ordinary SPI card reader with chip select on D10: use SdCard.begin() as-is. It shares no pins with the display or touch panel.

The touch panel shares its pins with the display bus (X- = display RS, Y+ = display CS, X+/Y- = data lines 0/1), so readTouch() temporarily reconfigures them and restores the display bus before returning. Touch coordinates are mapped with ELEGOO's published calibration for this panel; use calibrateTouch(int, int, int, int) (from touchRawX()/touchRawY() readings at the screen's edges) if a particular panel reports offset or mirrored positions.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public static void begin()
      Configures the shield's pins, resets and initializes the ILI9341 in 16-bit color, and selects PORTRAIT rotation, a size-1 white-on-black text style, and ELEGOO's default touch calibration. The screen contents are undefined until the first fillScreen(int).

    • setRotation

      public static void setRotation(int value)
      Selects PORTRAIT, LANDSCAPE, PORTRAIT_FLIPPED, or LANDSCAPE_FLIPPED. Coordinates, width()/height(), and touch positions all follow the current rotation. Existing screen contents are not redrawn.

    • width

      Current width in pixels, for the current rotation.

      Current height in pixels, for the current rotation.

    • beginPixels

      public static boolean beginPixels(int x, int y, int w, int h)
      Opens a wxh window with its top-left corner at (x, y) for streaming pixels with pushPixel(int), row by row from the top-left — the fast way to draw a small custom bitmap. Returns false, opening nothing, unless the window lies entirely on screen. Push exactly w * h pixels before any other drawing call.

    • pushPixel

      public static void pushPixel(int color)
      Writes the next pixel of the window opened by beginPixels(int, int, int, int).

    • setCursor

      public static void setCursor(int x, int y)
      Moves the text cursor so the next character's top-left corner is at (x, y) pixels.

    • setTextSize

      public static void setTextSize(int size)
      Scales text by an integer factor (1 = 6x8-pixel cells, 2 = 12x16, ...); values below 1 are treated as 1.

    • setTextColor

      public static void setTextColor(int foreground, int background)
      Sets the text foreground and background colors. Characters always paint their whole cell, so printing over older text replaces it — pad shorter strings with spaces to erase leftovers.

    • print

      public static void print(String text)
      Prints text at the cursor with the current text size and colors, advancing the cursor. '\n' moves to the start of the next text line, and text wraps at the right edge. Characters outside printable ASCII (32-126) are drawn as spaces.

    • print

      public static void print(int value)
      Prints value in decimal at the cursor.

    • print

      public static void print(byte[] buffer, int length)
      Prints the first length bytes of buffer as ASCII characters at the cursor, like print(String) — for text that already lives in a caller-owned byte buffer (e.g. Json.getString(byte[], int, String, byte[], int)'s output) and would otherwise need a runtime String.

    • println

      public static void println(String text)
      Prints text and then moves the cursor to the start of the next text line.

    • readTouch

      public static boolean readTouch()
      Samples the touch panel, returning whether it is currently pressed — only when two position and pressure samples agree, which rejects noise from the pins it shares with the display bus. When it is, touchX()/touchY() hold the pressed position in screen coordinates for the current rotation. Always leaves the display bus ready for drawing again.

    • touchX

      public static int touchX()
      X coordinate of the last successful readTouch(), for the current rotation.

    • touchY

      public static int touchY()
      Y coordinate of the last successful readTouch(), for the current rotation.

    • touchRawX

      public static int touchRawX()
      Raw 10-bit X reading of the last successful readTouch(), for calibration.

    • touchRawY

      public static int touchRawY()
      Raw 10-bit Y reading of the last successful readTouch(), for calibration.

    • touchPressure

      public static int touchPressure()
      Pressure estimate of the last readTouch() (0 when untouched; higher is firmer).

    • calibrateTouch

      public static void calibrateTouch(int rawLeft, int rawRight, int rawTop, int rawBottom)
      Replaces the touch calibration: the raw readings at portrait x = 0, x = 239, y = 0, and y = 319. Passing a larger "left" than "right" reading mirrors that axis.
